'''Nicholas José Talbot''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Biology|FRSB]] (born 5 September 1965) is a British biologist who currently serves as Group Leader and Executive Director at [[Sainsbury Laboratory|The Sainsbury Laboratory]] in Norwich.<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | title=TALBOT, Prof. Nicholas José | id = U250697 | volume = 2014 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]}}</ref><ref name=googlescholar>{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref name=orcid>Nick Talbot {{ORCID|0000-0001-6434-7757}}</ref><ref name=scopus>{{Scopus|id=7006917507}}</ref>

==Education==
Talbot was educated at [[Midhurst Grammar School]].<ref name=whoswho/> He went on to study at the [[Swansea University|University of Wales, Swansea]] for a Bachelor of Science degree in [[microbiology]], graduating in 1986. Following his undergraduate degree, he trained at the [[University of East Anglia|University of East Anglia (UEA)]] where he was awarded a PhD in 1990 for [[genetics|genetic]] and [[genomic]] analysis of the leaf [[Leaf mold|mould]] ''Cladosporuim fulvum''.<ref name=orcid/><ref name=talbotphd>{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Nicholas José|last=Talbot |title=Genetic and genomic analysis of Cladosporuim fulvum (syn. Fulvia fulva) |publisher=University of East Anglia |year=1990 |url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.253614|authorlink=Nick Talbot}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Professor Nick Talbot FRS FSB|url=https://biosciences.exeter.ac.uk/staff/index.php?web_id=nick_talbot|publisher=[[University of Exeter]]|access-date=2014-09-23}}</ref>

He was appointed [[Chancellor (education)|Deputy Vice-Chancellor]] for Research and Knowledge Transfer in 2010. In 2018, Talbot joined The Sainsbury Laboratory in Norwich as Group Leader and Executive Director.

Talbot is the editor of ''Molecular and Cellular Biology of Filamentous Fungi''<ref>{{cite book | last = Talbot | first = Nick | title = Molecular and cellular biology of filamentous fungi: a practical approach | publisher = Oxford University Press | location = Oxford New York | year = 2001 | isbn = 0199638373 }}</ref> and ''Plant-Pathogen Interactions''.<ref>{{cite book | last = Talbot | first = Nick | title = Plant-pathogen interactions | publisher = Blackwell Pub | location = Oxford | year = 2004 | isbn = 9781405147934 }}</ref>

Talbot's research has been funded by the [[Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council|Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC)]] and the [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council|Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC)]].<ref name="rcuk">{{cite web|url=http://gtr.rcuk.ac.uk/person/97B74465-8297-440F-9143-FAB7567CACFF|title=UK Government research grants awarded to Nicholas Talbot]|website=rcuk.ac.uk|publisher=[[Research Councils UK]]|access-date=24 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304110032/http://gtr.rcuk.ac.uk/person/97B74465-8297-440F-9143-FAB7567CACFF|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Talbot has twice been awarded prestigious [https://erc.europa.eu/homepage European Research Council (ERC)] Advanced Grants in 2013<ref>{{Cite web |title=Datahub of ERC funded projects |url=https://erc.easme-web.eu/?p=294702 |access-date=2022-12-05 |website=erc.easme-web.eu}}</ref> and 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-29 |title=Exciting research on plant infections awarded a multi-million euro grant |url=https://www.norwichresearchpark.com/exciting-research-on-plant-infections-awarded-a-multi-million-euro-grant |access-date=2022-12-05 |website=Norwich Research Park |language=en-GB}}</ref> His current ERC grant supports the SEPBLAST project which will build on his research group's recent discoveries on fungal morphogenetic proteins, called septins, being essential for the rice blast pathogen to cause disease.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Exciting research on plant infections awarded a multi-million euro… |url=https://www.tsl.ac.uk/news/exciting-research-on-plant-infections-awarded-a-multi-million-euro-grant |access-date=2022-12-05 |website=The Sainsbury Laboratory |date=27 April 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Talbot was elected [[Royal Society of Biology|Fellow of the Royal Society of Biology (FRSB)]] in 2010, a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] in 2013, and a [[Member of the Academia Europaea|Member of Academia Europaea (MAE)]] in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: Talbot Nicholas |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Talbot_Nicholas |access-date=2025-04-24 |website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref> He was also elected as a [[Fellow of the Royal Society|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS)]] in 2014. His nomination reads: {{centred pull quote|Nicholas Talbot is distinguished for his discoveries contributing to our knowledge of how fungi cause disease in plants. He has elucidated the molecular processes of cell differentiation and [[autophagy|autophagic]] [[cell death]] in fungi causing diseases such as [[Magnaporthe grisea|rice blast]]. He has shown how these processes are intimately involved in [[virulence]] and [[pathogenicity]] and are orchestrated to enable the complex cellular processes that enable a filamentous fungus to invade healthy plants. His work is characterised by a combination of [[molecular biology|molecular]], genetic, genomic and [[Cell biology|cell biological]] approaches.<ref name=royal>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/fellowship/2014/nicholas-talbot/ |title=Professor Nicholas Talbot FRS |publisher=royalsociety.org |archive-date=2014-09-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140924043127/https://royalsociety.org/people/fellowship/2014/nicholas-talbot/ |location=London |author=Anon |year=2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>}}

In 2025, Talbot was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science|Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2025-03-28 |title=AAAS names 2024 Fellows |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adx6365 |journal=Science |volume=387 |issue=6741 |pages=1363–1366 |doi=10.1126/science.adx6365|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
==Personal life==
Talbot is married to Catherine Ann Walsh, with two sons and one daughter.<ref name=whoswho/>
